scope: Integrity re-pin after merging the wave-2 governance branch (0b128db) onto main at the wave-0 squash (65e92df) on branch wave-2/integration. The merged packet carries wave 0's documentation edits and wave 2's release-1 authorization slice at the same time, so neither side's packet digest is correct for the merged tree and one re-pin is required. The wave-2 governance bytes are: two new scoped implementation authorization records (OBX-AUTH-R1-P1-SOLO-001, OBX-AUTH-R1-P2-SOLO-001) with their risk-exception amendments, the owner packet-acceptance record, two phase packet design documents, the release-1 and compatibility domain flips in the authority manifest, two plan-register rows, the relaxed registry id rule in scripts/verify-plan-authority.mjs, the new scripts/verify-r1-phase-authorization.mjs module, seven new negative tests in scripts/verify-plan-authority.node.mjs, and the P1 and P2 security and Grok 4.6 model receipts. No other packet input changed in this merge.

ownerDirection.pathListDerivation: The owner named no file. His words authorize the run's waves ('let's run zero through three') and accept the Release 1 packet ('I accept the release packet'). Run-contract section 5, wave 2, sets what wave 2 may do: 'Each phase gets its own scoped authorization record (paths, effect classes, prohibited capabilities, exact reviewer model) written from the master plan before code starts, and its own PR.' The exact allowedPaths, allowedEffects, and forbiddenEffects lists in OBX-AUTH-R1-P1-SOLO-001 and OBX-AUTH-R1-P2-SOLO-001 are derived from the wave-2 authorization plan written under that instruction (~/.claude/goal-state/one-box-gauntlet-r1/plans/wave-2-authorization-path.md, sections 1.4 and 4), which in turn cites docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-release-lifecycle-foundation.md, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-canvas-to-agency-shipping-design.md, and the Release 1 contract. They are a derivation from owner direction, not owner-dictated file lists.
ownerDirection.authorizationBoundaryStatedPlainly: The owner authorized running waves 0 through 3 and accepted the Release 1 packet. He did not name a packet re-pin; no owner ever does. This record must not be read as owner approval of a re-pin, and it grants no implementation authority of its own. The implementation grants live in the two registry records, which the verifier and the release-1 phase module check on every run.

It pins the first three registry records as exact bytes; requires nonWaivableClassesTouched to be empty; rejects broad or glob path scope; deep-equals governanceBindings and dependencyBindings to the frozen T02 values and hashes them live; hashes planBindings, the amendment, the predecessor files, and both receipts live; requires the parent ticket status to match the ticket manifest and stay inactive; enforces the 336-hour window, the self-hash, the Grok 4.6 model receipt identity, and the P2 predecessor-merge gate; and fails the whole module once OBX-AUTH-P180-T01-SOLO-001 or OBX-AUTH-P180-T02-SOLO-001 expires.

The file now holds 115 tests, all passing under GITHUB_ACTIONS=true npm run test:plans.

reEndorsement: This re-pin is an integrity refresh over a merge, not a new grant. It writes one packet digest and one T02 receipt digest so that the merged tree's recorded hashes match its bytes. The authority it sits beside is real and is stated plainly: the two release-1 phase records do carry implementationAuthorized true, and they are the first records to do so outside the OBX-P180 T01 and T02 pair. That authority comes from the registry records, their amendments, and the owner's packet acceptance, each reviewed on its own; this record neither creates nor widens it. The manifest still forces implementationAuthorized false at top level and on every domain, the two flipped domains gain owner-approved status with every grant withheld, target-topology and program-security stay proposed because their own documents block acceptance without an OwnerAssignmentV1, and no ticket status moved. Two properties are recorded on purpose. First, this record is not in the release-1 phase module's activationWriteSet constant, by design: the module lists the fifteen files an activation PR may write, docs/audits/ is excluded from the packet digest, and a re-pin record that named itself in its own governed write set would be circular. It is therefore unpinned by the phase records and stands on the verification evidence above. Second, scripts/verify-obx-p180-source-adoption.mjs remains red and unwired per ENGINE-LEDGER REPO-012; this re-pin moves the digests it hard-codes for the third time and does not repair it, because repairing it is a separate change the ledger already tracks.
